Thanks Ben / Sophie — I reviewed Novaline's redline and have annotated the attached 'transfer-impact-addendum-draft.pdf' with our suggested language. High-level summary:
1) SCCs — we are prepared to adopt the EU Commission standard clauses (latest release) but Novaline's counsel requested an addendum that modifies certain liability and processor-subprocessor routing obligations. We cannot accept substantive liability increases. We can agree to explicit routing and notification commitments (e.g., 30-day notice + mitigation plan) but not to unlimited indemnity.
2) Roles & Model Training — we will accept a strict "no customer content for model training" clause unless Novaline wants to enable a defined opt-in program (separate addendum + fees). Add opt-in language or a firm prohibition — your choice.
3) Transfer Impact Addendum — we can include a 24-month EU-only hosting commitment for initial onboarding with the caveat that we may rely on equivalent safeguards for backups and DR sites; we will document the fallback routing and escalation path.

Open asks from legal to procurement: please confirm whether Novaline expects operational geo-locking (technical enforcement) or contractual commitment only. If technical enforcement is required we'll need to involve infra and estimate cost/lead time.

I'm attaching the PDF with inline notes (transfer-impact-addendum-draft.pdf) and a copy of the SCCs annex we propose (SCCs_Annex_Novaline.pdf). If procurement is comfortable with the compromise language, we can prepare a consolidated DPA redline for signature.
